samples.summary: Read-only enforcement for the image-mutation path lives in the callee, not on the enforced entry path (`imageKeyHandler` is dispatched before `handleKeyDown`'s read-only guard)
samples.evidence: `TextEditor.handleKeyDown` consults `this.imageKeyHandler(e)` at text-editor.ts:864 and returns immediately when it reports the key consumed — that is *above* the read-only early-return at text-editor.ts:893. So every branch inside `imageKeyHandler` (editor.ts:2320-2387) executes with no shared permission gate, and the only thing standing between a viewer's Delete/Backspace and `doc.deleteText()` is the guard this diff added inside the callee (`if (readOnly || !selectedImage) return;`, editor.ts:2263). I traced all reachable branches and found no live bypass today: Escape and the arrow branches only move the caret, the catch-all returns false and falls into the read-only guard, cut is blocked earlier at text-editor.ts:1236, and `updateSelectedImage`/`insertImage` are additionally neutered by the read-only API allowlist at editor.ts:3851. The weakness is structural — the gate is now duplicated per mutating branch rather than enforced once at the dispatch point, so the next mutating key added to `imageKeyHandler` silently ships without it. Suggest gating the dispatch itself (e.g. only forward non-mutating keys to `imageKeyHandler` when `this.readOnly`).

samples.summary: Image copy/cut now writes document-authored `alt` text as the clipboard's `text/plain` flavour, which a co-author of a shared doc fully controls
samples.evidence: `writeImageToClipboard` sets `text/plain` to `image.alt ?? ''` (text-editor.ts:1297). `alt` reaches the model unvalidated from the clipboard sanitizer (`sanitizeImageData`, view/clipboard.ts:117-118 accepts any string, newlines included) and from HTML paste, so a malicious collaborator on a shared document can arrange that a victim who selects an image and presses Cmd/Ctrl+C ends up with arbitrary attacker-chosen multi-line text on the system clipboard while believing they copied a picture — the classic pastejacking setup if it is then pasted into a terminal. Impact is bounded: copying any ordinary text range in the same document already yields author-controlled text, so this does not create a fundamentally new capability, and browsers copying an image normally put nothing textual on the clipboard. Worth considering a single-line/length-clamped alt, or omitting `text/plain` entirely for an image-only copy.

samples.summary: The security rationale comment on `selectImageInline` overstates that nothing else focuses the hidden textarea in read-only mode
samples.evidence: The new doc comment (editor.ts:1244-1252) asserts "nothing else gives the hidden textarea keyboard focus — and a read-only editor never focuses on mount either". `TextEditor.handleMouseDown` calls `this.focus()` unconditionally at text-editor.ts:1699 — the read-only branch at 1660 only records a pending link href and falls through — so an ordinary canvas click already focuses the textarea for a viewer. Separately, in read-only `handleImageMouseDown` returns at editor.ts:2497, so the click-to-select-image path this comment describes cannot even run for a viewer; the only read-only entry is the `selectImageAt` API, which I found no frontend caller for (grep for `selectImageAt` under packages/frontend/src returned nothing). Nothing insecure follows — the focus adds no reachable mutation, since `handleInput` (1767), `handleCompositionStart` (691), `handlePaste` (1466) and `handleKeyDown` (893) are all read-only gated — but a wrong premise in a comment that justifies a permission-adjacent behaviour change is worth correcting before someone reasons from it.
